subtopic: Lock-Free Data Structures and Atomic Primitives
question_text: In lock-free algorithms utilizing Compare-And-Swap (CAS), what is the ABA problem and how is it resolved?

options.text: A value changes from A to B and back to A; resolved using versioned pointers or generation counters
A thread acquires lock A then B then A; resolved via mutex nesting
Memory addresses are swapped in cache; resolved with barrier instructions
Branch prediction failure; resolved with compiler unrolling

answer_explanation: A thread reads A, is preempted, another thread changes A->B->A. The first thread's CAS succeeds despite intervening structural changes. It is resolved using tagged/versioned pointers.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: A thread reads A, is preempted, another thread changes A->B->A. The first thread's CAS succeeds despite intervening structural changes. It is resolved using tagged/versioned pointers.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
